config.title: Props Drilling

intro.title: Props Drilling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that demonstrates props drilling, a technique for passing data from a parent component down to deeply nested child components. You will learn how to use Angular's @Input decorator to pass data through multiple layers of components. The core programming concept covered is component communication via input properties, which is essential for sharing state in a component tree. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of the data being passed. By the end, you'll understand how to implement and manage props drilling in an Angular project.
intro.usecase: Props drilling is essential in Angular applications when you need to pass data through multiple nested components without using a state management library. A common example is a dashboard where user preferences or filter selections need to be accessible by deeply nested chart components, sidebar widgets, and data tables. This pattern also appears in e-commerce product pages where product details must flow from the main product component down to variant selectors, quantity controls, and add-to-cart buttons. Understanding props drilling helps developers maintain data flow in medium-sized applications before implementing more complex state solutions.

objectives: Implement a parent component that passes data to child components through props
Configure nested child components to receive and display props from parent components
Construct a component hierarchy with three levels to demonstrate props drilling
Bind data properties from parent components to child component inputs
Update component props to reflect changes in the parent component's state
Manipulate component trees to visualize the flow of data through props
Initialize component properties with default values and override them through props

steps.title: Import Component and Input decorators from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import the Component and Input decorators from '@angular/core' to enable component creation and props drilling.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in both decorators from the Angular core package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing decorators from Angular
import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component and Input decorators are imported, making them available for use in your Angular component.
successCriteria: Component and Input are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both Component and Input from '@angular/core' using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect. You need to import both Component and Input from '@angular/core' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the ParentComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction:
Define a class named ParentComponent and decorate it with @Component, providing a selector of 'app-parent' and a template string containing '

Parent Component

'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator imported in the previous step to define the component metadata.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent class is defined with proper Angular component metadata.
successCriteria:
ParentComponent class exists, is decorated with @Component, has selector 'app-parent', and template contains '

Parent Component

'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the class is named ParentComponent, has the @Component decorator with selector 'app-parent', and template contains the heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incorrect. Check that you've defined the class with @Component decorator and proper metadata.

steps.title: Define initial data property in ParentComponent
steps.instruction: Inside the ParentComponent class, add a property named 'parentData' with an initial string value of 'Data from Parent'.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body, similar to: parentData = 'Data from Parent';
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent class now has a 'parentData' property that holds the initial data to be passed down.
successCriteria: The ParentComponent class contains a 'parentData' property with the string value 'Data from Parent'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check that it's named exactly 'parentData' and has the initial value 'Data from Parent'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ParentComponent class should have a property named 'parentData' with the value 'Data from Parent'.

steps.title: Create the ChildComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create a new component class named ChildComponent with the @Component decorator below the ParentComponent. Set its selector to 'app-child' and give it a template with a heading 'Child Component'.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as ParentComponent: use @Component decorator with selector and template properties, then export the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have two component classes in the file: ParentComponent and ChildComponent.
successCriteria: ChildComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-child', and template containing 'Child Component' heading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating ChildComponent, but make sure it has the @Component decorator with selector 'app-child' and a template with 'Child Component' heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent isn't properly defined. Check that you have the @Component decorator with correct selector and template.

steps.title: Add @Input() decorator to ChildComponent for receiving data
steps.instruction: Inside the ChildComponent class, add a property named 'childData' and decorate it with @Input() to receive data from the parent.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator above a property declaration to make it receive data from a parent component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will have an @Input() property ready to receive data from ParentComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the property declaration and the @Input() decorator above it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent doesn't have the required @Input() property. Check that you've added 'childData' with the @Input() decorator.

steps.title: Create the GrandchildComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create a third component class named GrandchildComponent with the @Component decorator below the existing ChildComponent. Set its selector to 'app-grandchild' and leave its template empty for now.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern used for ParentComponent and ChildComponent: use @Component decorator with selector and template properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a third component class ready to receive props from ChildComponent.
successCriteria: GrandchildComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-grandchild', and empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but check: did you include the @Component decorator with selector 'app-grandchild'?
steps.feedbackWrong: The GrandchildComponent class with @Component decorator is missing. Review how ParentComponent and ChildComponent were created.

steps.title: Add @Input() decorator to GrandchildComponent for receiving data
steps.instruction: Inside the GrandchildComponent class, add an @Input() decorator to a property named 'grandchildData' to receive data from ChildComponent.
steps.hint: Use the same @Input() decorator pattern you used in ChildComponent, but name the property 'grandchildData'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The GrandchildComponent will have an @Input() property ready to receive data through props drilling from ChildComponent.
successCriteria: GrandchildComponent has an @Input() decorator applied to a property named 'grandchildData'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the @Input() decorator to a property in GrandchildComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The GrandchildComponent doesn't have the @Input() decorator yet. Add @Input() to a property named 'grandchildData' in the GrandchildComponent class.

steps.title: Create ParentComponent template with ChildComponent selector
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent's template, add the ChildComponent selector (<app-child>) and bind the parentData property to the child's input property using property binding syntax.
steps.hint: Use the component selector as an HTML element and bind parentData to the child's input property with square brackets.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent template now includes the ChildComponent with data binding, establishing the first link in the props drilling chain.
successCriteria: ParentComponent template contains <app-child> element with [childData]="parentData" property binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct selector (<app-child>) and property binding syntax ([childData]="parentData").
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should include <app-child [childData]="parentData"></app-child> to bind data from parent to child.

steps.title: Create ChildComponent template with GrandchildComponent selector
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent's @Component decorator, add a template that uses the GrandchildComponent selector and passes the received childData to it using property binding.
steps.hint: Use the app-grandchild selector in the template and bind the grandchildData input property to childData.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent template now includes the GrandchildComponent selector with property binding, demonstrating props drilling from child to grandchild.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct selector and property binding syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should include the GrandchildComponent selector with property binding to pass childData.

steps.title: Create GrandchildComponent template to display drilled data
steps.instruction: In the GrandchildComponent template, add interpolation to display the received grandchildData value.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the grandchildData property in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The GrandchildComponent template will display the data passed through props drilling from ParentComponent to ChildComponent to GrandchildComponent.
successCriteria: GrandchildComponent template contains interpolation that displays the grandchildData property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using interpolation ({{ }}) to display the grandchildData property in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The GrandchildComponent template should display the grandchildData property using interpolation. Try adding {{ grandchildData }} inside the template.
